title: Outsiders made district heads over the Idoma
text: Before the Idoma had a paramount ruler, the British set district heads over their clans, several of them strangers: in 1907 Alabi, a Hausa-speaking Yoruba man from Ilorin, over Ugboju; in 1910 Momoh, a Nupe man, over Agatu at Obagaji; in 1911 Mallam Auta, a Hausa man, over Adoka. Awudu Elachi became district head of Otukpa in 1908. Customary courts followed in 1920 and the Idoma Native Authority in 1923.
